subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a triglyceride, the bond formed between glycerol and each fatty acid is:
options: a peptide bond
a glycosidic bond
an ester bond
a phosphodiester bond
questions.explain: Each fatty acid's carboxyl group condenses with a hydroxyl group of glycerol to form an ester bond, releasing water.

questions.q: During atrial systole, blood moves from the atria into the ventricles because:
options: Ventricular pressure exceeds aortic pressure
The atria relax and fill with blood
The semilunar valves open
Atrial pressure rises above ventricular pressure, pushing the AV valves open
questions.explain: Contraction of the atria raises atrial pressure above that of the ventricles, forcing the open AV valves to allow blood through.

questions.q: The secondary structure of a protein (alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet) is stabilised primarily by:
options: hydrogen bonds between the C=O and N-H groups of the backbone
disulfide bridges between cysteine R-groups
ionic interactions between R-groups
peptide bonds between adjacent chains
questions.explain: Secondary structure arises from regular hydrogen bonding between backbone carbonyl and amine groups, independent of R-group identity.

questions.q: A flatworm relies on diffusion across its body surface for gas exchange. Which feature of its body makes this possible despite having no specialised system?
options: A thick, impermeable cuticle
A flattened shape giving a large surface area and short diffusion distance to all cells
A high metabolic rate requiring rapid oxygen delivery
A closed circulatory system carrying haemoglobin
questions.explain: Its flat, thin body provides a large SA:V ratio and ensures no cell is far from the surface, so diffusion alone suffices.

questions.q: ATP is resynthesised from ADP and inorganic phosphate in a reaction that is:
options: a spontaneous exergonic process needing no enzyme
a hydrolysis releasing energy
an oxidation of glucose
a condensation requiring energy, catalysed by ATP synthase
questions.explain: Phosphorylation of ADP is an endergonic condensation reaction catalysed by ATP synthase, storing energy in the new phosphate bond.

questions.q: Why does a single circulatory system (as in fish) deliver blood to the body at a lower pressure than a double system?
options: Fish blood is more viscous
The heart has four chambers in fish
Fish have no heart
Blood passes through the gill capillaries before reaching the body, so pressure drops before systemic delivery
questions.explain: In a single circuit blood loses pressure passing through the gill capillaries, so it reaches the body more slowly than in a double system.

questions.q: A student tests a solution with Benedict's reagent and observes no colour change on heating, then performs the Benedict's test again after boiling with dilute acid and neutralising, obtaining a brick-red precipitate. This indicates:
options: a reducing sugar was present originally
a protein was present
a non-reducing sugar such as sucrose was present
a lipid was present
questions.explain: Acid hydrolysis breaks a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides, which then give a positive Benedict's result.

questions.q: Why is the tracheal system of an insect generally unsuitable for supporting a very large body size?
options: Diffusion of oxygen along long tracheae becomes too slow to meet demand deep in the body
Tracheoles fill permanently with fluid in large insects
Haemolymph cannot carry any oxygen
Spiracles cannot be closed in large insects
questions.explain: Because the system relies largely on diffusion, oxygen cannot reach deep tissues fast enough in a large insect, limiting body size.

questions.q: During ventricular systole, the atrioventricular valves close because:
options: The semilunar valves are open
Ventricular pressure exceeds atrial pressure
The ventricles are relaxing and filling
Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
questions.explain: As the ventricles contract their pressure rises above that of the atria, forcing the AV valves shut to prevent backflow.

questions.q: In the cohesion-tension theory of water transport, water moves up the xylem because:
options: Root pressure alone is sufficient in tall trees
Transpiration creates tension, and cohesion between water molecules pulls a continuous column upward
Active transport pumps water from root to leaf
Osmosis pushes water from the leaves down to the roots
questions.explain: Evaporation from leaves lowers pressure, and hydrogen-bonded cohesion lets a continuous water column be pulled up under tension.

questions.q: A property of water that makes it an effective coolant in transpiration and sweating is its:
options: low surface tension
high latent heat of vaporisation
low specific heat capacity
inability to act as a solvent
questions.explain: Water's high latent heat of vaporisation means much heat energy is removed when it evaporates, providing efficient cooling.

questions.q: Ringing experiments, in which a ring of bark (and phloem) is removed from a tree trunk, support the role of phloem in translocation because:
options: Water stops reaching the leaves above the ring
The leaves immediately wilt
Sugars accumulate in the bulge above the ring while tissues below may die
The xylem also stops functioning
questions.explain: Sugars cannot pass the removed phloem, so they build up above the ring, showing phloem carries organic solutes.

questions.q: During inspiration in a mammal, the pressure in the thorax falls because:
options: The diaphragm relaxes and domes upward
The external intercostal muscles relax
Surfactant reduces the surface tension of the alveoli
The volume of the thoracic cavity increases as the diaphragm flattens and the ribs move up and out
questions.explain: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure below atmospheric so air flows in.

questions.q: A polysaccharide gives a positive iodine test (blue-black) and on complete hydrolysis yields only alpha-glucose, including some from 1,6 bonds. The molecule is most likely:
options: chitin
cellulose
amylopectin
amylose only
questions.explain: Amylopectin stains blue-black with iodine and is a branched chain of alpha-glucose with both 1,4 and 1,6 glycosidic bonds.

questions.q: In the formation of a phosphodiester bond between two nucleotides, the bond forms between:
options: two phosphate groups directly
two nitrogenous bases
the phosphate group of one nucleotide and the deoxyribose of the adjacent nucleotide
the base of one nucleotide and the sugar of the next
questions.explain: A condensation reaction links the phosphate of one nucleotide to the sugar of the next, forming the sugar-phosphate backbone.

questions.q: Compared with elastic recoil in expiration, why are the walls of arteries elastic?
options: To stretch under high pressure and recoil, smoothing out pressure surges and maintaining flow
To slow blood flow for absorption
To allow active contraction that pumps blood
To enable exchange of materials with tissues
questions.explain: Elastic tissue in artery walls stretches during systole and recoils during diastole, evening out pulsatile pressure and sustaining blood flow.

questions.q: The semilunar (aortic and pulmonary) valves open when:
options: The ventricles relax during diastole
Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
Ventricular pressure exceeds the pressure in the aorta and pulmonary artery
The AV valves are also open
questions.explain: Once ventricular pressure rises above arterial pressure the semilunar valves open and blood is ejected.

questions.q: The wall of the left ventricle is thicker than that of the right ventricle because it must:
options: Generate a higher pressure to force blood around the entire systemic circulation
Pump blood only to the nearby lungs
Hold a larger volume of blood
Contract more slowly than the right ventricle
questions.explain: The left ventricle pumps blood through the high-resistance systemic circuit, requiring more cardiac muscle to generate greater pressure.

questions.q: Most tissue fluid is returned to the circulation by the:
options: Active transport across the capillary wall
Arteriole end of the capillary
Venule end of the capillary only, driven by osmosis
Combination of osmotic return at the venule end and drainage by the lymphatic system
questions.explain: Some fluid re-enters at the venule end down a water-potential gradient, and the excess is collected and returned by the lymphatic system.

questions.q: Hydrogen bonding between water molecules arises because water is:
options: a polar molecule with a partially negative oxygen and partially positive hydrogens
an ionic compound that dissociates fully
a non-polar molecule with even charge distribution
a hydrophobic solvent
questions.explain: Unequal sharing of electrons makes oxygen slightly negative and hydrogens slightly positive, allowing hydrogen bonds between adjacent water molecules.

questions.q: In a fish gill, the counter-current flow of water and blood is efficient because:
options: It allows carbon dioxide to be reabsorbed into the blood
Blood and water flow in the same direction, equalising oxygen quickly
A diffusion gradient for oxygen is maintained across the entire length of the lamella
Water flows faster than blood, reversing the gradient
questions.explain: Counter-current flow keeps the oxygen concentration of water higher than that of blood along the whole gill lamella, maintaining a diffusion gradient throughout.

questions.q: Cellulose differs from starch in that cellulose is composed of:
options: alpha-glucose with 1,6 branch points
alpha-glucose joined by 1,4 glycosidic bonds
beta-glucose with alternate molecules inverted, joined by 1,4 glycosidic bonds
beta-glucose joined only by 1,6 glycosidic bonds
questions.explain: Cellulose consists of beta-glucose monomers, with every other molecule rotated 180 degrees, allowing straight chains and hydrogen bonding between chains.

questions.q: Phospholipids form bilayers in water because:
options: both ends of the molecule are hydrophobic
the glycerol backbone repels water
they are entirely hydrophilic and dissolve fully
the phosphate head is hydrophilic and the fatty acid tails are hydrophobic
questions.explain: The amphipathic nature, a hydrophilic phosphate head and hydrophobic tails, drives self-assembly into a bilayer with tails facing inward.

questions.q: The primary structure of a protein refers to:
options: the alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets
the overall 3D folding stabilised by R-group interactions
the specific sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide
the association of multiple polypeptide subunits
questions.explain: Primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acids determined by the gene, dictating all higher levels of folding.

questions.q: In the condensation reaction forming a dipeptide, which statement is correct?
options: A hydrogen bond forms between two R-groups
A peptide bond forms between an amine group and a carboxyl group with loss of water
A glycosidic bond forms with release of water
A water molecule is added across the peptide bond
questions.explain: Condensation joins the amino group of one amino acid to the carboxyl group of another, forming a peptide bond and releasing water.

questions.q: The emulsion test for lipids gives a positive result shown by:
options: a blue-black colour
a brick-red precipitate
a purple/lilac colour
a cloudy white emulsion
questions.explain: Lipids dissolved in ethanol form a cloudy white emulsion when added to water, as the lipid disperses into droplets.

questions.q: The Bohr effect describes how an increase in carbon dioxide (and fall in pH):
options: Shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the right, so haemoglobin releases more oxygen at a given partial pressure
Has no effect on oxygen affinity
Shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the left, increasing haemoglobin's affinity
Increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood
questions.explain: Higher CO2 lowers haemoglobin's oxygen affinity, shifting the curve right so more oxygen is unloaded in respiring tissues.

questions.q: In a DNA nucleotide, the three components are:
options: glycerol, phosphate and a base
deoxyribose, sulfate and a base
deoxyribose, phosphate and a base
ribose, phosphate and a base
questions.explain: A DNA nucleotide consists of a deoxyribose pentose sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base.

questions.q: Which type of bond is NOT involved in stabilising the tertiary structure of a globular protein?
options: Ionic bonds between charged R-groups
Hydrogen bonds
Phosphodiester bonds
Disulfide bridges
questions.explain: Tertiary structure is held by hydrogen, ionic and disulfide bonds plus hydrophobic interactions; phosphodiester bonds link nucleotides, not amino acids.

questions.q: A phospholipid differs from a triglyceride in that a phospholipid has:
options: three fatty acids attached to glycerol
only ester bonds and no hydrophilic region
no glycerol backbone
one fatty acid replaced by a phosphate-containing hydrophilic group
questions.explain: In a phospholipid, one of the three fatty acids of a triglyceride is replaced by a hydrophilic phosphate group, making the molecule amphipathic.
